Narrow, well-scoped change: exposes the existing `DHCPService.get_kea_dhcp_data_for_agent` over the internal mTLS API. Service layer, exception mapping, and HAL response conventions are respected, and `ServiceCollectionV3.dhcp` already exists (src/maasservicelayer/services/__init__.py:279, 658), so the wiring is sound.

Main issues:

1. Authorization gap (security). `RequireClientCertMiddleware` only proves *some* enrolled agent is calling; it stores the cert CN in `request.scope["client_cn"]` (src/maasapiserver/v3/middlewares/client_certificate.py:45) and nothing binds that CN to the `{system_id}` path parameter. Any enrolled agent can therefore read another rack's full DHCP picture: host reservations (MAC/IP/hostname), gateways, next_server, DNS/NTP, and Kea HA peer IPs. `get_agent_config` has the same shape, but it only leaks a config the agent already owns; this endpoint leaks fleet-wide network inventory, and `get_kea_dhcp_data_for_agent` is query-heavy (src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py:118-405), so it is also an unauthenticated-by-rack DB amplification vector.

2. Redundant 422 declaration. `handler()` unconditionally injects `422: ValidationErrorBodyResponse` whenever `responses` is set (src/maasapiserver/common/api/base.py:35-40), so both the new entry and the new import are dead weight. The status actually missing from the docs is 403.

3. Response model duplicates the whole `DHCPDataForAgent` contract field-by-field; a field added to the dataclass is silently dropped from the API with no test failure.

4. No consumer: the Go agent client (src/maasagent/internal/client/client.go, src/maasagent/internal/dhcp/service.go:670) still uses `/agents/{system_id}/services/dhcp/config`, which proxies the legacy Django API. If this endpoint is meant to replace that path, say so in the commit body; otherwise it is unreachable code until the agent side lands.

5. Tests lean on framework behavior rather than handler logic — details inline.

Note (optional, [INFERENCE] about agent polling cadence): the sibling `get_agent_config` sets an `ETag`; if agents poll DHCP data periodically, a conditional-GET story would avoid re-running the whole query set per poll.

I could not execute the suite in this review environment (read-only tooling), so the test observations are from reading, not from a run.

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.15: This import is only needed for the redundant `422` entry below; `handler()` already injects it (src/maasapiserver/common/api/base.py:35-40). Drop both.
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.203: Redundant: `handler()` does `config["responses"].update({422: {"model": ValidationErrorBodyResponse}})` for every handler that declares `responses` (src/maasapiserver/common/api/base.py:35-40), so this entry is overwritten by an identical one. What *is* undocumented here is `403`, which `RequireClientCertMiddleware` returns with a bare `{"detail": ...}` body.
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.209: `system_id` is unbound from the caller's identity. `RequireClientCertMiddleware` sets `request.scope["client_cn"]` (the agent UUID) but nobody reads it, so any enrolled agent can fetch any rack's DHCP data — host reservations (MAC/IP/hostname), gateways, next_server and Kea HA peer IPs. Suggest taking `request: Request`, resolving the agent via `AgentsClauseFactory.with_uuid(request.scope["client_cn"])`, mapping `agent.rackcontroller_id` -> `node.system_id` (same lookup `get_agent_config` already performs) and raising `ForbiddenException` on mismatch. Related: siblings key on `{uuid}` (agent UUID) while this keys on the rack's node `system_id`; worth being explicit about which identifier agents are expected to send.
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.212: Unguarded fan-out: `get_kea_dhcp_data_for_agent` issues a long chain of queries (vlans, relay vlans, subnets, ipranges, interfaces, reserved IPs, static IPs, domains). With no per-caller binding and no ETag/conditional GET, a single misbehaving or hostile agent can drive this repeatedly for every rack.

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models.71: This re-declares the full `DHCPDataForAgent` shape. Any field added to the dataclass (src/maasservicelayer/models/dhcp.py:69-75) is silently absent from the API response and no test fails. Either nest the payload (`data: DHCPDataForAgent`) or build with `cls(**asdict(dhcp_data), hal_links=...)` so the contract stays in one place.
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models.94: Nit: `f"{self_base_hyperlink.rstrip('/')}"` — the f-string wrapper does nothing; `self_base_hyperlink.rstrip('/')` is enough. (Copied from `AgentConfigResponse`; fixing both is fine.)

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.87: `DHCP_DATA` is a module-level mutable dataclass graph shared across the class; a future test that mutates it leaks into others. Prefer a fixture/factory returning a fresh instance.
src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.368: This test does not exercise the new endpoint. `RequireClientCertMiddleware` short-circuits before routing, so it passes for any URL — including one that does not exist — and the `assert_not_called()` is therefore vacuous. The behavior is already covered by src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/middlewares/test_client_certificate.py. Recommend deleting.
src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.404: This and `test_agent_dhcp_data_404` both only assert `ExceptionMiddleware`'s exception->status mapping (src/maasapiserver/common/middlewares/exceptions.py:129-134), which is generic framework behavior; the handler has no branching of its own. Keeping one propagation test is enough. A test that would actually earn its keep: the caller/`system_id` authorization check suggested on the handler.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.42: Pure field-copy assertions (`response.vlans == dhcp_data.vlans`, etc.) fully subsumed by `test_agent_dhcp_data_200`, which additionally proves JSON serialization of the dataclass fields. Per AGENTS.md ("avoid trivial assertions", "keep tests minimal"), drop this class.
